title: 2027-01-11-acceptance-criteria-and-benchmarking-poc-sync-chasmware.json
summary: POC scoping focused on acceptance criteria, realistic workload sizing, throughput/latency benchmarks, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Key tradeoffs discussed: hosted vs dedicated vs private with emphasis on burst traffic, prefix caching, KV cache semantics, and encryption/KMS requirements. Action items include benchmark plan, security questionnaire, and draft SOW + pilot timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet template and runbook link
Customer to confirm representative dataset and 48-hour burst window details
Redwood SE to run initial throughput tests against 3 model configs and share numbers by 2027-01-21
Schedule tech deep-dive on private/VPC packaging after security questionnaire is returned
action_items: Ana Gomez (Redwood SE): create and run 3x throughput benchmarks (small/medium/large model) with synthetic burst profile; deliver CSV + charts by 2027-01-21
Samira Patel (AE): send pricing ranges for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and draft SOW skeleton by 2027-01-14
Marcus Lee (ChasmWare): provide sample request traces and token distribution (1 week) by 2027-01-18
Ellen Zhao (ChasmWare Security): complete Redwood security questionnaire and note KMS/HSM requirements by 2027-01-19
questions: What exact p95 latency is acceptable for user-facing chat?
Do you have hard cost limits per 1M tokens?
Is there a requirement for full data residency in EU/US?
Are there internal procurement timelines that would force Dedicated/Private?
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we have an hour, we'll aim to land on acceptance criteria and a concrete pilot plan
[00:08] Jordan (CTO): Thanks, yeah big picture is we want to replace our current on-prem microservice that does intent classification and routing. Latency is critical, but cost can't explode.
[00:22] Priya (Head of ML): quick note: our traffic is very bursty — marketing sends big campaigns, we see 10x baseline bursts for 2-6 hours. The KV cache behavior during prefix reuse matters a lot.
[00:35] Ana (Redwood SE): Got it. When you say KV cache, do you mean session KV for chat or prefix cache for repeated prompts?
[00:40] Priya: both, but prefix reuse is the bigger saver. Also we use a lot of short prompts (~30-80 tokens) but a few long ones coming from summarization flows.
[00:53] Marcus (Platform): current infra is k8s on Azure AKS, we can open peering/VPN for VPC. We also have a tokenization pattern that's fairly small per message but high QPS.
[01:02] Lee (Redwood): thanks, that helps. Two-dimensional decision: steady throughput vs burst capacity and data governance. Hosted gives easiest start, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, Private for full control and on-prem.
[01:16] Ellen (Security): on the security side, SOC2 is a must, we need audit logs, SSO/SAML, and HSM integration for keys. Any solution that can't integrate with our KMS is a no-go.
[01:27] Samira: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and can be deployed into customer VPC or on-prem box, but it adds 2-4 week setup time for pilot compared to hosted.
[01:37] Jordan: timeline is tight though — we want pilot results within 4 weeks, is Private realistic?
[01:42] Ana: realistic but more complex. Hosted or Dedicated can get you running in 3-5 days for a simple pilot; Dedicated with reserved capacity gives better control for burst but still requires network config and commit.
[01:55] Priya: what about caching and quantization — do you have recommendations to avoid quality regressions?
[02:02] Lee (Redwood): Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles by workload; we typically start with fp16 or int8q and run eval sets to detect regressions. We'll include a quality-preserving quant baseline in the benchmark plan.
[02:15] Marcus: curious about p95 targets — our SLA for user chat is 300ms p95. Can Redwood hit that with hosted?
[02:23] Ana: depends on model size and region. For a compact 7B-ish decoder with prefix cache enabled, we've seen 200-350ms p95 in hosted for short prompts. For larger models it's higher. We'll validate with your token distribution.
[02:35] Jordan: cost — we currently have cost target of <$10 per 1k user requests (rough heuristic), but want per-token numbers too.
[02:44] Samira: we'll provide per-token estimates and tradeoffs. Dedicated dramatically reduces unit cost at scale because of reserved GPU pools and better batching. Hosted is higher per-token but no infra overhead.
[02:56] Priya: acceptance criteria — proposal: (1) p95 latency <= 350ms for chat flow (short prompts), (2) degradation <= 5% quality vs baseline on evaluation prompts, (3) survive 10x burst for 2 hours with tail latency < 1.2s, (4) integration with our KMS and audit logs present.
[03:18] Samira: that list is great. We'll formalize it into 'POC acceptance tests' — smoke tests + perf + quality checks.
[03:25] Jordan: benchmarks — we need a benchmark script that can replay our traces including variations in token lengths and session reuse. Marcus will handover trace.
[03:31] Marcus: yes I can export tsv with timestamped requests and tokens distribution.
[03:36] Ana: for throughput tests we'll spin up three configs: small model (quant int8), medium (fp16), large (fp16/bswap) — each with steady and burst phases. We'll capture p50/p90/p95/p99, GPU util, and cost per token.
[03:53] Priya: can you do prefix caching toggle? We need to see the delta.
[03:57] Ana: yes we'll run caching on/off. Note that on Redwood Dedicated there's more control over cache sizing.
[04:04] Lee (Redwood): a note on routing: if you pick Hosted initially we can still route to Dedicated for burst via policy, but that requires pre-approved model variants and failover policies.
[04:15] Jordan: about failover — if Dedicated pools are saturated, will hosted fallback keep latencies acceptable?
[04:22] Ana: fallback is possible but you'll see a latency delta — the playbook is to have a lighter-weight model in hosted as a graceful degrader. We'll document expected deltas.
[04:33] Ellen: encryption-at-rest plus customer-managed keys is required; do you support HSM-backed KMS?
[04:39] Samira: yes Redwood Private supports HSM integrations; Hosted supports KMS with envelope encryption but HSM-backed requires Private or Dedicated with customer-managed key proxies. We'll put specifics in the security pack.
[04:54] Marcus: procurement — if we need Dedicated we have procurement cycles that add 3-5 weeks. That pushes pilot beyond 4 weeks.
[05:02] Priya: could we do hybrid — start Hosted for initial functional QA and then replicate to Dedicated for perf window?
[05:08] Ana: that is a common pattern: two-phased pilot. Phase 1 (hosted) for functional + quality in 3-5 days, Phase 2 (dedicated load/perf) once traces + commitment provided.
[05:20] Jordan: Ok let's sketch timeline: Week 0 (this week) — agree acceptance tests + handover traces. Week 1 — hosted functional run and quality eval. Week 2 — Redwood runs benchmarks (steady + burst). Week 3 — dedicated pilot (if commit) or extended hosted run. Week 4 — finalize SOW and decide go/no-go.
[05:41] Samira: agreed, we'll draft a SOW with those milestones. We'll also include a rollback/fallback policy and cost estimate scenarios.
[05:49] Ana: technical notes for the benchmark: we'll simulate 48-hour trace but compress into burst windows to accelerate. We'll provide CSV with columns: timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, session_id, cache_hit_bool.
[06:02] Marcus: we also need logs and tracing hooks — can Redwood emit distributed traces to our Zipkin/Jaeger?
[06:10] Lee (Redwood): yes, we can ship traces to a customer endpoint; we also have per-request metadata in the console for debugging.
[06:20] Ellen: auditing: need immutability on logs and retention policy — can you set retention to 7 years for some artifacts?
[06:27] Samira: long retention is an add-on; we can scope it in the SOW as enterprise observability retention.
[06:35] Jordan: benchmarks — what's the expected GPU footprint for our worst-case burst?
[06:40] Ana: based on your QPS estimate (which Marcus will provide), we'll size GPU pools. For a 10x burst for 2 hours, Dedicated with autoscaling + burst buffer is recommended to avoid cold starts. We'll simulate both cold-start and warm-cache cases.
[06:56] Priya: one more on quality — we need A/B eval between current baseline model and candidate models using our eval set, scoring F1 and semantic similarity; target is <= 5% drop.
[07:09] Ana: we'll run those evals and include confusion matrices. We'll also test tokenization drift.
[07:18] Jordan: procurement/contract — can Redwood provide a short-term reserved seat for Dedicated for pilot to reduce unit cost without long-term commit?
[07:25] Samira: yes, we have short pilot reserved capacity offers — they'll reduce cost but do have a minimum. I'll include numbers in the pricing doc.
[07:36] Marcus: integration work — how invasive is the SDK? We want to minimize changes to our orchestration layer.
[07:42] Lee (Redwood): SDK is lightweight; for private/VPC we provide a sidecar and a small runtime shim. For hosted it's just API calls. We'll share example integration snippets.
[07:53] Ellen: cross-tenant data leakage question — if we pick hosted, how do you guarantee isolation between customers?
[07:59] Ana: multitenant hosted isolates at the model runtime level and we use namespace separation; logs and data at rest are partitioned. For stricter needs Dedicated/Private provide physical or VPC isolation. We'll put the exact isolation model in the security doc.
[08:14] Jordan: great. Let's confirm deliverables: benchmark plan + run, security questionnaire, SOW draft, and an initial pricing range.
[08:22] Samira: yes. We'll also share example benchmarks from similar customers (anonymized) and a benchmark template on Google Sheets.
[08:30] Priya: timeline again — please push the benchmark results by 2027-01-21 so we can review before procurement window.
[08:36] Samira: that's doable. Ana and Lee will lead the bench.
[08:41] Marcus: handover — I'll upload traces to the secure share and grant access to Redwood by EOD 2027-01-12.
[08:47] Ellen: security questionnaire — expect to receive it by 2027-01-13.
[08:51] Samira: closing — we will email the SOW skeleton and pricing, link to benchmark runbook, and schedule the deep-dive if needed. Thanks all.
[08:58] Jordan: thanks, bye.
[09:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "fp sixteen" spelled out as words sometimes. Speaker attribution has been normalized where possible but still shows informal labels. Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks-template (shared after call), security pack link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (placeholder).
